explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration stating this strong maximum principle for harmonic functions. I listed every theorem and lemma in Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Harmonic and Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Harmonic. They cover mean values (circle averages), Poisson kernels, Liouville, analyticity of harmonic functions, and basic constructions; none is a maximum principle. I also grepped all of Mathlib for lines that mention harmonic functions together with IsLocalMax, IsMaxOn or IsLocalMin, and got no matches. Mathlib's maximum-modulus results for holomorphic functions (e.g. Complex.eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn_norm) are stated for norms of holomorphic maps. Getting this theorem from them would mean building a local holomorphic function whose real part is f and other steps, which is more than one or two lines. The current proof relies on the library's own lemma eqOn_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_le_of_eq, plus Mathlib's HarmonicAt.analyticAt and the identity theorem for analytic functions (AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq).
